attrs.evidence: H = {a,b,c},{a,b} with site 1 holding the Sym(D)-invariant ternary 'a = b' and site 2 holding a ≠ b. GYO reduces it (α-acyclic); every sub-hypergraph is α-acyclic (β-acyclic); two edges cannot form a γ-cycle. It is Berge-cyclic, both sites are satisfiable, and the union is not. Sampling agrees: α-acyclic unions violate fidelity thousands of times per run.
attrs.prior_art: Fagin 1983 states the mechanism — two hyperedges sharing ≥2 vertices are already Berge-cyclic, which is exactly why database theory weakened the notion. For a local-satisfiability certificate that weakening is unaffordable.
attrs.statement: α-, β- and γ-acyclicity of the union hypergraph are sufficient carriers for the local-satisfiability certificate.
